title: Intel Stock (INTC) Falls 8.1% as Chip Stocks Retreat (Nov 24)
summary: Intel stock (INTC) fell 8.15% to $54.80 on November 24, 2026, as chip stocks gave back Monday's rally after Nvidia brought back Jensen Huang as CEO.
body_markdown:
## Why Intel Stock Fell


The sources reviewed for this article name no new Intel announcement on Tuesday. Financial media tied the drop to a reversal in chip stocks after Monday's rally.


On Monday, November 23,[Nvidia's decision to bring back CEO Jensen Huang](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/nvidia-nvda-stock-news-november-24-2026/) set off a huge rally across chip stocks, as reported by The Motley Fool. That rally reversed sharply on Tuesday as investors digested what his return will mean in the long term and how it will affect chip rivals such as Intel, the outlet said.


Per[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-november-24-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-chip-stocks-nvidia-140629923.html) , semiconductor stocks declined on Tuesday alongside other areas of the AI trade as worries about a December rate hike returned to focus. Yahoo Finance also reported that Micron gave back some of its double-digit gains from Monday.


The Motley Fool also pointed to last week's foundry news. Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the company had landed its first outside customer for 18A-P, an advanced manufacturing process, but details were light, so its financial impact is unclear, according to the outlet.


## INTC Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Intel's first outside customer for 18A-P is a positive step for a process The Motley Fool calls important to the company's turnaround efforts.
- According to[Zacks](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/top-analyst-reports-apple-philip-205300421.html) , improving yields and lower wafer costs strengthen Intel's production economics.
- Zacks also says multiyear cloud collaborations support the Xeon roadmap, while server demand and advanced packaging are widening customer engagement.


### Risks


- Intel's foundry business posted a $1.85 billion operating loss last quarter, and the finance chief indicated the company probably won't generate positive[free cash flow](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/free-cash-flow-and-net-cash-flow-explained-2/) next year, per The Motley Fool.
- Zacks flags the PC correction, memory shortages and factory disruption as constraints on sales and margins.
- Competition, China exposure, heavy capital commitments and equity dilution complicate the recovery, according to Zacks.
